thread:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER -> sam. Alert: 3x GPU OOMs on decode-pool-14 (10.2.4.7) in 90s. Error pattern: CUDA out of memory during streaming decode. Auto-throttle kicked, ~120 requests dropped in last 5m. Severity: P2.

sam: seeing it in the dashboard, CPU fallback launched but high latency. Repro rate ~15% for a particular customer shard.

kira: which shard? any correlation with max_tokens header?

sam: looks like requests with max_tokens=4096 and no stop sequence; one customer traffic spike sending long prompts. Their average seq len ~20 -> suddenly long.

mike-runtime: logs:```
[2026-03-15T18:01:20Z] decode_stream: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY alloc 6.2G
[2026-03-15T18:01:20Z] node-14: container restart (OOM)
[2026-03-15T18:01:21Z] inference-proxy: dropped 24 requests due to pool depletion
```

jess-support: customer-ops on call, @customer-ops pinged. Which customers affected?

customer-ops: confirmed: AcroHealth (acct: AH-42) saw 502s and timeouts. They reported loss of chat continuity. Impact window ~18:00–18:06 UTC.

sam: immediate mitigation plan: 1) apply token cap on frontend for that shard (enforce max_tokens <= 512), 2) scale decode-pool by +2 nodes (if capacity available), 3) route new sessions for AH-42 to fallback smaller model / CPU path with warning banner.

kira: +1 on token cap. We should also enable prefix KV caching exception to avoid full context reloads.

mike-runtime: scaling attempt: `resize-pool decode-pool-14 --add 2` -> quota shows 0 GPUs left in region. autoscaler not allowed to expand. fallback plan: restart a couple of idle nodes to reclaim GPU memory and evict bad containers.

sam: I'll trigger a rolling restart on pool-14 to evict hung processes. Command:```sh
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deploy/decode-pool-14 --timeout=5m
```

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: started rollout restart: deploy/decode-pool-14 (requested by sam)

kira: while rollout runs, apply runtime guard to reject requests with token header >512 with 429 and quick error message. Patch config:```json
{"routing": {"shard_policy": {"AH-42": {"max_tokens": 512, "fallback": "cpu-small"}}}}
```

mike-runtime: putting guard into prod via feature-flag: `ff on enforce-token-cap-AH42` -> rolling to edge proxies now.

sam: monitoring drops: initial drop rate falling from 120 -> 18/min after proxy guard. CPU fallback latency: 600–1200ms extra, acceptable.

jess-support: filed a customer incident: noted that we applied temporary token cap and routing to fallback. Messaging to AcroHealth: short note that we throttled very long generations to protect cluster & will follow up. Assigning case to Kira for postmortem comms.

customer-ops: asking if there was any data leakage or incorrect completions?

kira: no evidence of data leakage. This is resource exhaustion only. All logs scrubbed per compliance.

mike-runtime: root cause quick analysis: a heavy batch of streaming requests with unbounded generation + incorrect client max_tokens header bypassed our previous front-end checks (bug: header ignored when `stream==true`). That allowed unlimited decode loops until GPU memory grew and driver threw OOM, container restarted.

sam: immediate TODOs captured: 1) Hotfix front-end to always validate max_tokens for streaming requests (patch #PR-8123), 2) Add server-side hard cap in runtime to enforce per-request token budget, 3) Improve autoscaler visibility for reserved capacity so we don't hit zero-GPU in-region, 4) Run replay of AH-42 traffic in staging and run load test.

kira: PR-8123 is small, I'll open and request review. Sam, can you add the runtime guard ticket?

sam: opened runtime ticket -> RUNTIME-2198. Adding a temporary linchpin to reject >1k tokens at runtime until proper quota checks shipped.

mike-runtime: after restart the pool shows nodes back, OOMs stopped. Current error rate normalizing. Monitoring windows: observe 10m for regressions.

oncall-bot: incident timeline note created: 2026-03-15T18:01Z GPU OOMs -> token cap applied 18:03Z -> pool restart 18:06Z -> customer routing 18:07Z.

jess-support: I'm drafting customer note: mention that we applied a temporary token cap and routed sessions to smaller model to restore service, apologize for disruption, include ETA for follow-up.

kira: postmortem checklist: include root cause (header bypass on stream), mitigation steps (proxy guard + runtime cap), engineering action items (PR-8123, RUNTIME-2198), and business impact (AH-42 6 minutes degraded). Also add runbook update: ensure frontend validates max_tokens for streaming.

mike-runtime: follow-up items for SLOs: consider automatic per-client token budgets and throttle policy when a single shard is anomalous.

sam: final check: are we happy to close page? any open customer blockers?

customer-ops: AcroHealth accepted the temporary mitigation and will await the postmortem. They asked for a targeted SLA credit assessment.

jess-support: noted. I'll own the credit calc with finance.

oncall-bot: pager cleared by sam at 1759815605.

sam: closing thread, will follow up with a short postmortem draft within 24h. Thanks all. :handshake:
